messages:
Sam (Zenith): Hi CS/Eng team — during our pilot rollout we9re seeing a sharp spike of 429s on the /v1/preflight endpoint when a scheduled push wakes a large subset of devices. About 30-50% of wakeups get a 429 within 30s of app start.

Maya (CS): Oof. Thanks for reporting, @Sam. Quick questions: which SDK and platform, are these ephemeral tokens or long-lived keys, and are you doing any bulk sync on boot?

Sam (Zenith): SDK 2.0.0-beta on Android (mix of 10/11). We mint a short-lived ephemeral token on first run and then refresh periodically. On wake we kick off a small sync which does a preflight per active account. The issue mostly happens right after a rich push goes out to many users.

Omar (Eng): Sounds like a simultaneous-token-mint + preflight fanout. Two leads: client connection reuse and token refresh de-dup. If every client establishes a new TLS connection and then immediately hits preflight, edge rate windows see a huge burst.

Sam (Zenith): We do not currently reuse our OkHttp client across wakes; each worker spins a fresh client for the job. We also do not gate token refreshes if multiple jobs race.

Omar (Eng): There are a couple of low-friction mitigations: (1) reuse a singleton HTTP client to keep connections warm, (2) add randomized start jitter when responding to push, (3) limit concurrent preflight calls per device process. Example knobs: reuseHttpClient=true, startJitter=rand(0,2500)ms, concurrencyLimit=4. Pseudo-code:

```
// single shared client
object Net { val client = OkHttpClient.Builder().connectionPool(ConnectionPool(5, 5, TimeUnit.MINUTES)).build() }

suspend fun scheduledSync() {
  delay(Random.nextLong(0, 2500))
  semaphore.withPermit { Net.client.newCall(preflightRequest()).execute() }
}
```

Maya (CS): I'll propose an onboarding mitigation: ask Zenith to flip the SDK flags and run a small canary. If that doesn't lower 429s, we can request a temporary tenant preflight threshold increase for the rollout window and enable coalescing on staging first.

ops-bot: Tenant flag changed: preflight_coalesce=enabled for tenant=zenith in staging at 2026-03-29T14:05:00Z. Metrics to watch: preflight_429_rate, preflight_success_rate, edge_conn_count.

Sam (Zenith): Great — we'll change the client to reuse the OkHttp instance and add 0-2.5s jitter and a max of 4 concurrent preflights. One question: should we honor Retry-After if the service returns it? We're sometimes seeing 429s with empty headers.

Omar (Eng): Yes, honor Retry-After when present. But because some 429s come from local edge rate policies without Retry-After, the client should implement exponential backoff with randomized jitter (initial 500ms, factor 2, max 8-10s). Also check that your token refresh logic uses in-flight dedupe to avoid N identical refreshes: keep a map of device->Deferred and await if a refresh is already ongoing.

Sam (Zenith): We'll implement inflight dedupe and backoff. Any server-side improvements we could request to make onboarding smoother?

Omar (Eng): We can enable a short-lived leniency window for your tenant during the rollout (48h), and temporarily raise the burst allowance on the edges that serve your region. We'll only do this for limited windows and with monitoring. If you expect >100k devices waking, we'll need a phased rollout schedule.

Maya (CS): I'll coordinate a 24-48 hour leniency window contingent on a canary pass. Sam, please post cohort results with these headers: x-edge-node, request-id, x-device-id, and client handshake time. Include sample 429 traces if still happening.

Sam (Zenith): Will do. Starting canary tonight with the client changes. Thanks everyone, will report back tomorrow morning.

Omar (Eng): One final tip: check DNS TTLs and whether the client frequently resolves to the same edge. Slightly increasing DNS spread or preferring different resolver options can spread TLS handshakes across more edges and reduce hotspotting.

Sam (Zenith): Noted. We9ll try reducing aggressive DNS caching on the client SDK. Appreciate the help!
